summary: Maine Forest Service tower in Baxter State Park, in use by 1919, restored 1989, removed 1999; only concrete footings remain, seen on a hiking trail.

facts.design: 12-foot steel tower with a tower house and a cabin (1919 report and 1920 inventory)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1999; concrete footings remain on the summit

staffing.status: staffed in 1919 (watchman, lookout and patrolman); no later staffing found in the sources read

access.note: Summit reached on foot by a trail in Baxter State Park; no closure or permit described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Trail starts about 0.5 miles from the Matagamon Gate at a small parking area; about 1.6 miles to the summit; the only view is from the East Spur Overlook

facts.agency: Maine Forest Service (built and staffed); Baxter State Park Authority (removed the tower in 1999)

events.note: Watchman, lookout and patrolman at the Horse Mountain cabin; bedroom added in June; tower house painted inside and out
Alidade and range finder installed at Horse Mountain to help locate fires
Six-man Wheelabrator volunteer crew flown in by a Maine Forest Service helicopter in July 1989; new windows, roof and floor; steel tower painted. Park had targeted the tower for return to service.
Baxter State Park Authority had the tower removed; firetower.org says it was torn down and burned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The regional register (firetower.org) says the tower was torn down and burned in 1999; the Eastern US Lookouts page and Maine by Foot say it was removed in 1999. Both agree on the year; the story says the sources differ on how it was taken down.

notes_for_editor: Built date is not in any source read; the story starts at the 1919 record. Height 3.7 m comes from the 1920 inventory figure of 12 feet (no later height). The 1989 restoration text and the 1999 removal are quoted secondhand on the Eastern US Lookouts page (originally Bangor Daily News), not checked against the original article. Summit elevation differs between hiking sources (1,589 ft vs 1,592 ft) and is not used. The brief's agency field is kept as Baxter State Park with the Maine Forest Service as builder.
